**Generated:** 2026-09-04T20:57:46.880Z · **Commit:** 623d3796 · **Nodes:** 183

One shared harness for every AI agent. Godkit puts a committed .agent/ directory in a repo - board, thread, map, sprints, tasks, logs - and teaches Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Antigravity to read it before editing and write to it before finishing, so work is not redone and two agents never edit one file. A zero-dependency Node CLI plus sixteen skills, published as @codeforfee/godkit. The CLI owns only what a machine can decide; everywhere judgment starts, it stops and hands off to a skill.

**Stack:** JavaScript

## Architecture

### Shared protocol and state

AGENTS.md and the committed .agent/ contract every host reads: board, thread, brief, sprints, tasks, logs, map. One canonical copy of each fact, with the host rule files generated from it.

- `AGENTS.md` — The canonical always-on protocol every host reads, and the only copy worth editing - the Claude, Cursor, Codex and Copilot rule files are generated from it and byte-compared in CI. Now also states the model-identity rule, which is where that rule actually gets enforced on hosts with no hook support.
- `CLAUDE.md` — Generated Claude-facing copy of AGENTS.md. It carries the full shared-state and file-ownership protocol so Claude sessions receive it without relying on hooks alone; edit AGENTS.md and regenerate instead of changing this file.
- `.agents/rules/godkit.md` — Generated Antigravity-facing copy of the canonical AGENTS.md protocol. It is byte-for-byte rule content for a host with no hook enforcement, so changes belong in AGENTS.md and the sync generator.
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — Generated GitHub Copilot-facing copy of the canonical AGENTS.md collaboration rules. It exists as a host adapter and must be regenerated from AGENTS.md rather than edited independently.
- `templates/BOARD.md` — One screen of current truth: roster, claims, task index, bugs, binding decisions, handoffs. The roster names MODELS with tools as a second column, because cost and capability belong to the model. Carries the current sprint id on one line.
- `templates/THREAD.md` — Append-only inter-agent message template for timestamped, attributed, task-linked actionable communication, including recipients and blockers.
- `templates/task.md` — Plan, Execute, Review, Test, Handoff, with scope and a checkable exit in frontmatter. owner: is a model id once claimed. Same generated-into-the-skill arrangement as log.md.
- `templates/log.md` — One log file per session - the reason two tools writing at once never conflict. agent: must be a model id. Its frontmatter is generated into godkit-handoff by scripts/sync-templates.js, so this file is the single source for the format.
- `templates/BRIEF.md` — Stands in for MAP.md on a project with no code yet. Non-goals is the load-bearing section: on an empty repo it is the only thing stopping an agent from inventing scope.
- `templates/sprint.md` — A goal and a wave table. The worked example is inside an HTML comment on purpose - a blank form teaches less than a filled one - which is exactly why lib/sprint strips comments before reading task ids.

### The contract - what counts as done

The rules the templates state, made checkable, plus the identity rule that says a log is signed by a model and never by a tool. Structural only, on purpose: judging whether evidence is good stays with godkit-review.

- `lib/contract.js` — The rules godkit already wrote down, made checkable. .agent/tasks/ and .agent/log/ were write-only until this existed: a task could sit at done with nothing behind it. Structural only - present, non-empty, not the template placeholder. Whether evidence is any GOOD stays with godkit-review, deliberately, because a fuzzy check would train agents to write around it.
- `lib/identity.js` — Who wrote this, in the only terms that stay true: the model, not the tool it ran inside. 'claude' is four different models with four different failure modes, and a year from now it is four others. Deliberately NOT a registry of known ids - a shipped allowlist is wrong within a quarter and then rejects the truth, so this only refuses what is definitely not a model id and lets the model name itself.
- `tests/contract.test.js` — Every contract rule against the sentence that states it, including no-identity on tasks and logs and the fact that the shipped log template does not pass its own checks as done.
- `tests/identity.test.js` — Pins the rule that a tool name is not an identity, across every vendor, plus the 'unrecorded' sentinel and the fact that why() never suggests it.

### Work organisation - seams and sprints

A task is one seam; a sprint is a goal plus waves of file-disjoint tasks behind a join gate. The CLI owns only what a machine can decide here; cutting the waves is the model's job.

- `lib/sprint.js` — A sprint is a goal plus waves of file-disjoint tasks. This does only the half a machine can do: find the sprints, resolve the task ids the wave table names, and say whether every one is finished with evidence behind it. Reuses lib/contract for the checking rather than growing a second frontmatter parser that would immediately disagree with the first.
- `tests/sprint.test.js` — Pins the refusals: a wave table naming a task nobody wrote, an unfinished task, a done task with no evidence, an empty sprint - and that the shipped template's commented example names no real tasks.
- `skills/godkit-plan/SKILL.md` — Cutting a task into seams on file boundaries, each with scope, exit and verification, then writing them out and claiming one.
- `skills/godkit-execute/SKILL.md` — The five-stage pipeline, and retry only on verified advancement.

### Session runtime

Host-neutral primitives for hook input and per-session state, isolated by session id under a godkit-owned directory and replaced atomically.

- `lib/session.js` — Host-neutral hook input and per-session runtime state. Session ids are hashed before they become path components and state lives only under a godkit-owned directory, so one session can never read or clear another. Also the atomic writer (temp + fsync + rename, optional compare-and-swap and .bak) that every config write in the package goes through.
- `lib/work.js` — Session-owned evidence that a tool changed project files — the thing clockout judges. Shell tools compare a before/after Git fingerprint that excludes .agent/, edit tools mark work only for successful paths outside it. A dirty working tree is deliberately NOT evidence: it says nothing about which session made it.
- `lib/lazy.js` — Centralizes lazy-mode configuration, runtime state, host-specific hook output, and instruction loading. Runtime mode is stored in one host-wide .godkit-lazy-active file, so concurrent sessions currently share and overwrite the same state.

### Hook enforcement

Where the protocol stops being advice on Claude Code and Codex: the session brief in, the clock-out block on the way out. Hooks never throw.

- `hooks/brief.js` — SessionStart: injects a bounded view of the shared state - board, map freshness, project skills, the two newest logs, the thread tail. Every section has its own byte budget so a large BOARD cannot starve the rest. The closing reminder is the one sentence injected into EVERY session, so it carries only what cannot be dropped: claim your scope, sign with your model, write your log.
- `hooks/clockout.js` — Stop: a session that changed project files keeps blocking until its own exact-session log exists. Judges the session, not the directory - someone else's dirty file is not evidence about you. Enforces exactly one contract rule (a done log with an empty ## Verified); the filename it suggests carries a <your-model-id> placeholder rather than a guessed tool name.
- `hooks/work-track.js` — The lifecycle hook that feeds work evidence: pre captures a fingerprint, post compares, edit records a direct edit, end clears the session. Registered on PreToolUse, PostToolUse and SessionEnd — without it nothing records work and clockout can never fire.
- `hooks/map-watch.js` — PostToolUse (Bash) hook. After a command that lands a change, says whether the map went stale — and stays quiet otherwise, because a warning that fires constantly gets muted.
- `hooks/lazy-activate.js` — SessionStart hook that resolves the godkit-lazy mode for this session and injects its ruleset. Mode state is per session, under the owned state root.
- `hooks/lazy-subagent.js` — SubagentStart hook. Inherits the parent session's lazy rules; a malformed matcher fails closed and warns rather than broadening its own scope.
- `hooks/lazy-mode-tracker.js` — UserPromptSubmit hook tracking /godkit-lazy switches and deactivation for the session.

### Install and ownership

What godkit owns on a machine and nothing else. Refuses any destination it did not create, and does not rewrite a settings file that already says the right thing.

- `lib/install.js` — What godkit owns on this machine, and nothing else. installOne refuses a destination it did not create; removeOne keeps what is not ours and says so. writeSettings is a temp-and-rename compared against the bytes it read, and is a NO-OP when the new body is byte-identical - without that, re-registering identical hooks renamed a file over the user's live config every time, which on Windows is an EPERM as soon as two processes land together (B-014).
- `lib/managed.js` — A managed block is godkit's few lines inside a file the user also owns. init used to skip any host file that already existed, which silently meant "this project gets no rules"; overwriting would have eaten the user's text. Marked blocks do neither, and ambiguous or hand-edited markers are refused rather than guessed at.
- `hooks/install.js` — Standalone hook registration for a settings file: a thin CLI over lib/install.js with --uninstall and --dry-run. Paths derive from where this file actually lives, so moving the package is a re-run rather than a text hunt.
- `scripts/uninstall.js` — Removes what a host's own uninstall cannot see: installed skill directories, hook registrations, and the session-state root. Shares every ownership decision with lib/install.js, so what install created is exactly what uninstall removes — nothing else.
- `tests/hook-install.test.js` — Install idempotence and the ownership rule. The two bugs it exists for: matching our entries by package name (which matched nothing, so re-runs appended), and filtering whole groups (which took a user hook out with ours).

### CLI and the map pipeline

The entry point, and the deterministic half of the map: walk, categorize, resolve imports, batch, then load-patch-save. The judgment half lives in agents/ and godkit-map.

- `bin/godkit.js` — The CLI, and the deterministic half of everything: init, install, hooks, scan, save, sprint, skills, evolve, refactor, verify, doctor, uninstall, --version. Every command that needs judgment stops at the point where judgment starts and hands off to a skill.
- `lib/scan.js` — Deterministic filesystem scanner that categorizes authored files, applies hard skips plus a documented subset of .agentignore/.gitignore, and regex-extracts resolvable relative imports. Unknown types and files over 400 KiB are intentionally absent from the map input.
- `lib/batch.js` — Greedy deterministic clusterer for semantic-analysis calls. It favors import-connected files, then same-directory neighbors, under a 60 KiB budget while guaranteeing every non-data file is placed once even when one file exceeds budget.
- `lib/graph.js` — Persistence and projection layer for project memory: guarded graph loading, portable path sanitization, node/edge normalization, saving, structural signatures, and generated MAP.md rendering. Node IDs are identity, duplicate nodes resolve last-wins, and dangling edges are dropped.
- `lib/freshness.js` — Is the map still true? staleness() is git-only and safe on every session start; classify() decides how much to rebuild. It fails CLOSED: an unreadable status, a meta sha the repo no longer has, or a failed diff all report unknown or stale — never fresh. A hook that blesses a map nobody verified is the one wrong answer.
- `lib/paths.js` — Locating shared project state. .agent/ belongs to the MAIN worktree so it survives linked worktree removal, and every read below it is bounded and refuses symlinks - a project-controlled link must not turn a session brief into a local-file reader. One exported real() canonicalizer, because two spellings of one directory compared as different and made Windows CI red for a week (B-012). Now also carries brief and sprints paths.
- `agents/file-analyzer.md` — Prompt and schema contract for turning one scan batch into graph nodes and observed edges. It requires every assigned file to be read, stable relative-path IDs, actionable summaries, no guessed relationships, and exactly one scratch JSON output.
- `agents/architect.md` — Prompt contract for the architecture synthesis pass after batch graphs are merged. It derives project metadata, 3-8 named layers, and a 5-9 step start-here tour without inventing framework or runtime claims.

### Skills and evidence

The sixteen shipped skills, the project-local ones in .agent/skills/, and the trust derived from the log stream alone - a usage/outcome correlation, never a quality score.

- `lib/evolve.js` — Project skills in .agent/skills/: what they are, whether they are safe to project into a host path, and what the log stream says about each. Projections are owned SHA-256 snapshots, not live links, so godkit replaces only what it wrote and never removes a foreign target. Trust is derived from logs alone — there is no separate store.
- `lib/hotspots.js` — Which code files the log stream says are hot: claimed in `scope:`, listed under `## Did`, or named as a root cause under `## Bugs`, cross-referenced against the map for fan-in. Reads no source code and scores no file the map does not know, so prose that merely looks like a path cannot rank. The deterministic half of godkit-refactor.
- `skills/godkit/SKILL.md` — The arrival protocol and the sprint loop: read .agent/, refresh a stale map, cut seams on file boundaries, claim scope, run waves behind a join gate.
- `skills/godkit-handoff/SKILL.md` — The .agent/ file formats and the clock-in / clock-out checklists. Its task and log frontmatter blocks are GENERATED from templates/ by scripts/sync-templates.js - edit the template, not the skill.
- `skills/godkit-plan/SKILL.md` — Cutting a task into seams on file boundaries, each with scope, exit and verification, then writing them out and claiming one.
- `skills/godkit-map/SKILL.md` — Building and refreshing this map. Says which of SKIP/PARTIAL/ARCHITECTURE/FULL to do, and why writing only fresh entries over the whole graph fails silently.
- `skills/godkit-git/SKILL.md` — Worktrees as the backstop for a board claim, commit as checkpoint, and why .agent/ rarely conflicts.
- `skills/godkit-execute/SKILL.md` — The five-stage pipeline, and retry only on verified advancement.
- `skills/godkit-lazy/SKILL.md` — Two ladders - fewest turns, then least code. lib/lazy injects this whole body into every session AND every subagent, so its LENGTH is a per-session cost, not a per-trigger one. That is why it is kept short.
- `skills/godkit-test/SKILL.md` — What counts as verified, and the smallest check that fails if the logic breaks.
- `skills/godkit-refactor/SKILL.md` — Ranking code files by churn and blame from the log stream, then reading them. Evolves SOURCE; godkit-evolve evolves procedures.
- `skills/godkit-output-enforcement/SKILL.md` — Locking a deliverable count so generated output is not handed over stubbed or truncated.
- …6 more

### Release guards

The generated files that cannot be edited in the wrong place, the version agreement across four manifests, and the pack check - a runtime file missing from the files allowlist works in a checkout and 404s for everyone else.

- `package.json` — Published as @codeforfee/godkit - the bare name is permanently refused by npm as too similar to the existing god-kit. Zero runtime dependencies, node >=18, and a files allowlist that is the real risk here: a runtime file missing from it works in a checkout and 404s for everyone who installed.
- `scripts/sync-rules.js` — Generates every host's always-on rule file from AGENTS.md, adding Cursor frontmatter only where required. --check turns the same projection into a CI drift detector.
- `scripts/sync-hooks.js` — Generates hooks/godkit-hooks.json from the HOOKS list in lib/install.js; --check fails if it drifted. A generated manifest cannot disagree with the installer, which is exactly how work-track came to be missing from one of them.
- `scripts/check-versions.js` — Every version-bearing manifest must carry the same version, and on a tag push that version must equal the tag. An empty or non-release tag now fails instead of skipping the check — the case where skipping is most dangerous.
- `tests/package.test.js` — Contract tests: the package ships what the README promises, manifests agree, generated files are current, and — the one that catches an allowlist bug — the packed file set can actually run godkit init from a temp directory.
- `README.md` — The product page, and what npmjs.com renders. Carries the install paths, the sprint loop, the model-identity rule, and the reference depth folded into <details>. Images use absolute raw URLs so they render on npm as well as GitHub.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — Release history. 1.0.0 is the first public release.

## Start here

1. **AGENTS.md - the protocol itself** — Two rules, the clock-in/clock-out checklist, and the model-identity rule. Every other rule file in the repo is generated from this one, so it is the only copy worth reading or editing.
2. **bin/godkit.js - where execution begins** — One switch, one command per concern. Read cmdInit first: it is the whole install story, including why the machine half runs at most once.
3. **lib/contract.js - what 'done' has to mean** — The templates always stated the rules; nothing read them back until this. Structural checks only, and the reason that boundary is deliberate.
4. **lib/sprint.js - a goal, and waves that do not collide** — Note what it does NOT do: it never invents tasks. The machine resolves ids and checks evidence; cutting the waves is judgment and stays with the model.
5. **hooks/brief.js and hooks/clockout.js - the enforcement** — Where the protocol stops being advice. Brief injects the shared state on the way in under a strict byte budget; clockout blocks the turn on the way out if this session changed files and wrote no log.
6. **lib/paths.js - the safety floor everything stands on** — Bounded, symlink-refusing reads below .agent/, and one canonicalizer. Two spellings of one directory once made Windows CI red for a week.
7. **lib/install.js - owning only what you created** — Refuses a destination it did not write, and will not rewrite a settings file that already says the right thing. Both rules exist because of a real bug.
8. **package.json and scripts/ - the release guards** — Four manifests must agree on the version, four rule files are generated and byte-compared, and npm pack --dry-run is the only check that catches a runtime file missing from the allowlist.

## Recall

Grep `.agent/graph.json`, never load it whole: search `"name"`, `"summary"` and `"tags"`
for the concept, collect the node ids, then grep those ids in `"edges"` for the one-hop
neighbourhood. That answers most questions without reading a single source file.
